1. Map Widget, Basemaps & Projections

Source: vignettes/basemaps-and-projections.Rmd
basemaps-and-projections.Rmd

Initializing the Map Widget

In glmap, you initialize a map with glmap() (or leaflet() when running legacy scripts) and chain layers and camera controls using the native R pipe |> (or %>%):

library(glmap)

# Initialize a dark GPU map centered on Montreal
glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
  set_view(lng = -73.5673, lat = 45.5017, zoom = 11)

Supported Input Data Sources

Unlike leaflet (which only accepts sf, sp, data.frame, or 2-column matrices), glmap() natively accepts all modern R spatial and zero-copy columnar formats without pre-conversion:

  • sf and sfc objects (POINT, MULTIPOINT, LINESTRING, MULTILINESTRING, POLYGON, MULTIPOLYGON) — automatically transformed to EPSG:4326 if projected.
  • terra::SpatRaster, stars, RasterLayer, or numeric matrix — streamed as raw Float32 values (GLMR binary packet) to a WebGL2 RGBA32F texture.
  • terra::SpatVector, sp::Spatial*, and maps::map() objects.
  • wk::xy, wk::wkb, and wk::wkt geometry vectors.
  • nanoarrow_array / GeoArrow streams.
  • data.frame, tibble, data.table, or 2-column numeric matrix — auto-detects lon/lng/long/longitude/x and lat/latitude/y columns.
  • crosstalk::SharedData — enables linked brushing across HTML widgets.

Basemaps & Tile Providers (set_basemap, add_provider_tiles, gl_providers)

glmap ships with built-in Vector GL styles (rendered at 60 FPS by MapLibre GL) and global XYZ raster tile providers:

# Short built-in basemap aliases
glmap(basemap = "dark")       # CARTO DarkMatter Vector GL
glmap(basemap = "positron")   # CARTO Positron Vector GL
glmap(basemap = "voyager")    # CARTO Voyager Vector GL
glmap(basemap = "osm")        # OpenStreetMap standard raster tiles
glmap(basemap = "satellite")  # Esri World Imagery satellite tiles
glmap(basemap = "topo")       # OpenTopoMap topographic tiles
glmap(basemap = "none")       # Blank canvas (pure WebGL2 data)

Using the gl_providers (or providers) Catalog

Just like leaflet::providers, type gl_providers$ (or providers$) for IDE auto-completion across 44+ vector and raster styles:

glmap() |>
  add_provider_tiles(gl_providers$OpenFreeMap.Liberty) |>
  set_view(lng = 2.3522, lat = 48.8566, zoom = 12)

# Inspect all built-in providers and their environment variables
head(gl_list_providers(), 12)
#>                      provider       type api_key_required api_key_optional

#> 2                    positron  vector_gl            FALSE             TRUE

Configuring Optional Provider API Keys (gl_set_api_key)

For commercial tile providers (MapTiler, Stadia/Stamen, Thunderforest, Jawg, Mapbox, or enterprise CARTO/Esri), configure keys once per session or via environment variables (MAPTILER_API_KEY, STADIA_API_KEY, MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN):

gl_set_api_key("maptiler", Sys.getenv("MAPTILER_API_KEY"))

glmap() |>
  add_provider_tiles(gl_providers$MapTiler.DatavizDark)

OGC Web Map Service (WMS) & Cloud-Native PMTiles / MVT

Stack real-time weather radar WMS layers (add_wms_tiles() / addWMSTiles()) or serverless .pmtiles archives (add_pmtiles()):

glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
  set_view(lng = -73.5, lat = 45.5, zoom = 6) |>
  add_wms_tiles(
    base_url = "https://geo.weather.gc.ca/geomet",
    layers = "RADAR_1KM_RRAI",
    transparent = TRUE,
    opacity = 0.75,
    group = "MSC Weather Radar"
  )

Camera, 3D Terrain & Globe Projection

Because glmap is powered by MapLibre GL + WebGL2, you can tilt (pitch), rotate (bearing), enable 3D DEM terrain extrusion (set_terrain()), or switch to a 3D spherical globe (set_projection("globe")):

glmap(basemap = "satellite", projection = "globe") |>
  set_terrain(exaggeration = 1.5) |>
  fly_to(lng = -122.19, lat = 46.20, zoom = 11, pitch = 60, bearing = -25)
